title: 2023 AMC 10B Problem 21
statement: Each of \(2023\) balls is randomly placed into one of \(3\) bins. Which of the following is closest to the probability that each of the bins will contain an odd number of balls?

solutions.text: All \(3^{2023}\) assignments are equally likely. A sign filter counts the ones with every bin odd: \(\frac{1}{8}\sum_{s \in \{\pm 1\}^3}(s_1 s_2 s_3)\) \(\cdot (s_1 + s_2 + s_3)^{2023}.\) For \(s = (1,1,1)\) and \(s = (-1,-1,-1),\) both terms equal \(3^{2023}.\) For each other sign choice, the sum in parentheses is \(1\) or \(-1,\) and the full term equals \(-1,\) so these six terms total \(-6.\) Thus the count is \(\frac{2 \cdot 3^{2023} - 6}{8} = \frac{3^{2023} - 3}{4}.\) Dividing, the probability is \(\frac{3^{2023} - 3}{4 \cdot 3^{2023}} = \frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{4 \cdot 3^{2022}},\) a hair under \(\frac{1}{4}.\) Thus, E is the correct answer.
hints: Encode “odd count” in each bin with a \(\pm 1\) sign filter, replacing oddness by \(\frac{1 - (-1)^k}{2}\)
